title: T5 Paginate Compare at 50 rows after global sorting
description: Create one request-local row model per filtered canonical model, sort and scale the complete filtered set, then clamp and slice a fixed 50-row page.
action: Set Compare-local PAGE_SIZE = 50. Build each filtered row once with identity, release/context, four current-currency prices, and board records; stable-sort the complete row array with missing numeric values last and name tie-break, compute maxima from that complete array, then clamp page and slice. Preserve default AAIndex-desc and explicit sort=none.
implementation: Resolve index, price, and board data only during candidate/row construction; comparators, maxima, and cell rendering consume the row object and never repeat lookups.
Parse positive page, compute total pages, clamp it, render at most 50 rows, report complete filtered/total and selected-column counts, and render existing Pagination.
Build pagination hrefs retaining q, owner, board, ability, cols including none, and explicit sort=none or valid sort/order; all state-changing forms omit page.
After implementation, add focused cross-page ordering, missing-last, maxima, clamping, retention, desktop/mobile overflow, pagination accessibility, and axe browser evidence.
convergence_criteria: [UI-observable] Compare tbody renders at most 50 rows and Pagination appears when filtered count exceeds 50.
Adjacent-page boundary assertions prove complete-set ascending and descending sorting before slicing, with missing numeric values last.
The same value has the same bar scale on different pages because maxima use the complete filtered row set.
Pagination retains q, owner, board, ability, cols, sort=none or sort/order and clamps invalid/oversized page values.
Desktop and mobile show local table overflow only, accessible pagination, and 0 serious or critical axe violations.
